entries.title: Icon requests: own API with developer tokens on Neon Postgres
entries.summary: Owner: an icon request "is not really an issue", so requests move off GitHub issues into our own API. A developer registers with an email and gets a token; the token is used to submit requests and to list and follow their statuses ("ubaci token i vidiš"). Leaked tokens are low risk: they only reveal which icons were requested and their status.
entries.spec: Neon Postgres via the Vercel Marketplace (DATABASE_URL set by the integration), queried with @neondatabase/serverless, no ORM. Tables: api_keys (id, email, token_hash = SHA-256 of the token, created_at, revoked_at) and icon_requests (serial id, key_id, name, description, keywords, status open|in-progress|declined, decline_reason, created_at, updated_at). Tokens look like vl_<32 random bytes base64url>, are shown once and stored only as a hash. Endpoints: POST /api/keys {email} -> 201 {token}; POST /api/requests (Authorization: Bearer) -> 201 {id, status, statusUrl}; GET /api/requests -> the token's requests with statuses; GET /api/requests/{id} -> status, only for the owning token. Done still comes from the published npm manifest (entry.request = request id), which keeps the manifest format; only the meaning of the number changes from issue number to request id (no icon-request issues exist yet, so nothing to migrate). Rate limits move from per-instance memory to the database: keys per IP per hour, requests per token per hour. Validation (parseIconRequest) stays; the Markdown stripping for issues can go. Removes GITHUB_TOKEN usage and apps/web/src/lib/github.ts. Risks: Neon cold start (~0.5 s on the first query after 5 min idle); email is not verified in this phase. Out of scope: web form, admin page, email delivery (see #request-web-ui, #request-email-notifications).
entries.plan: 1. Create the Neon database through Vercel Storage and pull env vars locally. 2. SQL migration file for both tables. 3. Token helpers (generate, hash, read Bearer header) with tests. 4. Rewrite the requests routes and add /api/keys. 5. Admin status change via an endpoint guarded by ADMIN_TOKEN until #request-web-ui adds the page. 6. Update README API section and docs/icon-definition-of-done.md (request = request id). 7. Release minor. Done: Neon (fra1, no preview branches, DATABASE_ prefix; functions moved to fra1), apps/web/db/schema.sql + db:migrate, lib/api-keys.ts, lib/db.ts, /api/keys, /api/requests (POST, GET list), /api/requests/[id] (GET, admin PATCH), github.ts removed. Limits: 3 tokens/hour per IP, 5 requests/hour per token. Local dev uses the production database.
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED v0.2.0, 2026-10-28] Production checked: 401 without token, token issued, request stored and listed; check rows removed. ADMIN_TOKEN still to be set on Vercel by the owner; until then PATCH answers 401.

entries.title: Icon requests on the website: get a token, submit, track, admin
entries.summary: The site on Vercel needs a form for new icon requests and a page where a developer pastes their token and sees what they asked for and its status. entries.spec: Pages on the existing Next.js app. /admin: login with ADMIN_TOKEN (httpOnly cookie holding its SHA-256, 30 days), token usage stats (active tokens, distinct emails, tokens that made requests), token list with request counts and revoke, all requests with email, description, keywords and status; status change via server actions. New stored status ready = drawn and added to the library, waiting for the npm release (owner wants to mark work as done and added); done stays automatic from the npm manifest so the API never reports an icon that cannot be installed yet. /request (get a token by email, then submit a request with it) and /requests (paste token, list of own requests; token kept in localStorage as a convenience only) use the same API endpoints as developers. Out of scope: email notifications.

Link from the home page. 7. Release minor. entries.title: Request an icon straight from /request-icons: token by email, form, own statuses
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-28: on https://vectilume.vercel.app/request-icons add a form so a user can send a request right on the web; they first give their email, get the token shown on the page, save it, and use it to follow their statuses. Owner, 2026-10-28: the user reaches the list "upisivanjem tokena ili svoje mail adrese" and sees only what they submitted, never anyone else's, unless they are the admin. Email access must not let someone who knows another person's address see their requests, so the owner chose a magic link (see #request-email-notifications).
entries.spec: Client section on /request-icons above the curl guide, calling the same API as developers (one validation path, same limits: 3 tokens/hour per IP, 20 requests/hour per token). Step 1: email -> POST /api/keys; the token is shown once with a copy button and a clear 'save it now' note, and kept in localStorage on that browser as a convenience (it is the only copy we hand out; the server stores just the hash). Step 2: request form (name, description, keywords) -> POST /api/requests with the token, field rules shown inline, API error messages shown as returned. Step 3: 'My requests': paste or reuse the stored token -> GET /api/requests, list with status, reason when declined, icon name and version when done; 'use another token' clears it. Admin: GET /api/requests with Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN> returns every request with its email, so the owner can use the same screen. Name field suggests kebab-case from free text. Icons from the Vectilume set only. Risks: token lost when localStorage is cleared and not saved (no email delivery yet, see #request-email-notifications); a browser on a shared IP may hit the tokens-per-hour limit. Out of scope: email sign-in (magic link, needs email delivery: #request-email-notifications), editing or deleting a request.
entries.plan: 1. Token step with copy and localStorage. 2. Request form. 3. My requests list. 4. Check on phone width and both error paths (400, 429). 5. Release minor. Done: RequestForm.tsx on /request-icons (email -> token with copy, paste token, request form with kebab-case name, list with statuses), token remembered in localStorage only when it is a developer token; admin branch in GET /api/requests.
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED v0.4.0, 2026-10-28] Checked locally against the production database: token issued and shown, 400 and 429 messages shown, request stored and listed, a second token sees neither the list entry nor GET /api/requests/{id} (404), invalid token returns to sign-in, admin token lists all requests with emails and is not stored, no horizontal scroll at 390 px; check rows deleted. Production /request-icons serves the form. Email sign-in waits for #request-email-notifications.

entries.title: Tokens only after email confirmation; a confirmed token sees every request of its email
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-28, after a new token showed none of his 8 requests: everyone with an email should be able to see their requests, "ali mora ići potvrda na mail da netko drugi ne traži token za njih". Owner chose Resend with a domain to be bought, and tokens delivered only after confirming the email (decides #token-email-verification as go).
entries.spec: POST /api/keys {email} stops returning a token once email is configured (RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM set): it stores a one-time code (SHA-256 only, 15 minutes) and mails a link to /request-icons?confirm=<code>, answering 202 {sent: true} whether or not the address is known. Limits: 3 per hour per IP and per email. The page posts the code to POST /api/keys/confirm (POST, so mail scanners that open links do not use it up), which issues a token marked verified (api_keys.verified_at) and shows it once. A verified token lists and reads every request made by any token of the same email; unverified older tokens keep seeing only their own. Resend is called over its HTTP API, no SDK. Plain-text English email. Without the env vars the old direct token stays, so the site keeps working until the domain exists; in development the link is logged instead of sent. Risks: until the domain is bought and DNS verified nothing changes in production. Out of scope: the other emails of #request-email-notifications, revoking old unverified tokens.
entries.plan: 1. Schema: api_keys.verified_at, email_confirmations table. 2. lib/email.ts (Resend fetch, dev log). 3. /api/keys sends the link when configured; /api/keys/confirm. 4. Email-wide listing for verified tokens in GET /api/requests and /api/requests/{id}. 5. Page: 'check your inbox' state and ?confirm handling. 6. Docs (page, icon-requests.md, README). 7. Release minor. 8. Owner: buy domain, Resend account, DNS, RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM on Vercel; then check the flow in production.
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED v0.5.0, 2026-10-28] Migration applied by the owner. Checked locally against the production database: confirm issues a verified token (201), reused, unknown and 16-minute-old codes refused (400), the verified token lists and reads the older request of its email and gets 404 for another email's request, the other token still sees only its own; the ?confirm link in the browser shows and stores the token and drops the code from the URL; check rows deleted. Production answers on /api/keys/confirm. Domain vectilume.dev (www primary) on Vercel and Resend DNS records in place (DKIM, send, DMARC). Still direct tokens: RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM not set yet; the mailed path of POST /api/keys is untested until they are. [EMAIL LIVE 2026-10-28] Owner set RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM (Vectilume <noreply@vectilume.dev>) and redeployed. First send failed with 403 (domain not verified): the send record had been replaced with MX/TXT on a wrong hint; Resend now uses CNAME send -> send.forge.rmta.net and CNAME rsend -> rsend-euw1.forge.rmta.net. After verification: POST /api/keys answered 202, the email reached the owner's Gmail, the link issued a verified token that lists all 8 of the owner's earlier requests.

entries.title: Emails for icon requests: token, request received, status changes, shipped
entries.summary: Developers should be told when a requested icon is delivered, not only find out by polling. Owner, 2026-10-28: add email sending tomorrow "pa da dobiju na mail svi info" (moved up from 2026-11-11, together with #request-form).
entries.spec: Resend (free plan) from a domain we own; the API key in RESEND_API_KEY on Vercel. Emails: (1) token on registration (POST /api/keys and the #request-form token step), so a token saved nowhere else is not lost; (2) request received, with id, name and a link to follow it; (3) status change made in /admin (in-progress, ready, declined with reason); (4) done: after an npm release, compare the published manifest's request ids with requests not yet notified, send icon name, version and the import line, store notified_at; a Vercel cron (daily) or a check on admin load triggers it. Plus 'resend my token' by email: issues a new token, revokes the old one, mails it (rate limited), since only hashes are stored. Plain, short English emails with the Vectilume name, no tracking. A failed send never fails the API call; it is logged. Risks: needs DNS access to the sending domain (SPF/DKIM); without a domain Resend only delivers to the account owner, so this item becomes blocked. Out of scope: email preferences or unsubscribe beyond a one-line note, HTML templates.
entries.plan: 1. Decide the sending domain (owner). 2. Resend account, DNS records, RESEND_API_KEY on Vercel. 3. lib/email.ts with the four messages. 4. Hook into /api/keys, POST /api/requests and the admin status action. 5. notified_at column and the done check (cron). 6. Resend-token endpoint. 6b. Sign in by email on /request-icons (owner, 2026-10-28, chose magic link over showing requests for any typed address): POST /api/sessions {email} mails a one-time link valid 15 minutes (only a hash stored, rate limited per email and IP, same answer whether the address is known or not); opening it lists every request made with any token of that email. 7. Update /request-icons, icon-requests.md and README. 8. Release minor. [2026-10-29] Steps 1, 2, 6 and 6b are covered by #request-email-confirm: Resend on vectilume.dev; 'Continue with your email' mails a one-time link that issues a new verified token, which lists every request of that email. Left: request received, status change and shipped emails (3-5), docs (7), release (8). Emails go only to addresses confirmed at least once (any verified token of that email), so the older unconfirmed tokens cannot mail a stranger. Shipped emails: done_notified_at column, a daily Vercel cron plus a button in /admin for right after an npm release; requests already done before the launch are marked notified without an email. [2026-10-29, owner] Developers may not want these emails: they can turn them off and follow requests on the page or through the API instead. email_settings per address (notify, stop-link code); a switch on /request-icons for tokens from a confirmed email; GET/PATCH /api/settings {emails}; a stop link in every request email that opens a page with a button (POST, so mail scanners change nothing), plus List-Unsubscribe one-click headers. The confirmation email is not affected. Ships with #request-review-flow.
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED v0.6.0, 2026-10-29] Received, status-change and shipped emails; daily cron /api/cron/shipped at 08:00 UTC registered on Vercel, CRON_SECRET set; nothing had shipped by request yet, so no backfill was needed. Checked in production: the received email reached the owner's Gmail. [v0.7.0, 2026-10-29] Emails can be turned off (page switch, /api/settings, stop link with List-Unsubscribe). Checked on test request #22: accepted, in-progress and ready emails arrived, the stop link turned emails off for the owner's address (email_settings.notify = false); #22 deleted afterwards. The shipped email is not tried in production yet: it needs an npm release with a request id.

entries.title: Codex reports its work on icon requests; owner approves drawn icons in /admin
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: icons for requests are drawn by Codex in a terminal; the terminal should always set the statuses itself, the owner only looks at the result and approves it with a button, after which it is planned for the next deploy. The SVG is enough as a preview. The owner decides when the npm release happens, so /admin should say how many icons are done and wait for it. Later the same day: new requests must first be accepted by the owner in /admin; accepted ones go to a folder Codex works from, and leave it when done.
entries.spec: Stored statuses now open (new, waiting for the owner) -> accepted (owner's OK, queued for Codex, public and emailed) -> in-progress -> review -> ready. New stored status review (drawn by Codex, waiting for the owner); developers keep seeing in-progress and get no email for it. A separate WORKER_TOKEN (Vercel env) for Codex: list the queue (accepted and in-progress requests (name, description, keywords, owner's change note, no emails), set in-progress, or set review with the icon id and its outline/duotone/solid SVGs (each up to 20 KB, must start with data URLs (no script runs), Approve (to ready, emails the developer) and Request changes with a note (back to in-progress, no email, the note goes to Codex). Root script `pnpm request [id]`: sync writes icon-queue/ (gitignored, one Markdown file per queued request, with the owner's change note), review removes the file; it finds the icon by its collection entry "request": id, reads the SVGs from packages/icons-svg/src and calls the API with VECTILUME_WORKER_TOKEN from a gitignored .env.worker; it prints what changed. AGENTS.md tells Codex to run it at the start and end of every request. Out of scope: Codex publishing to npm, previews on a deployed site.
entries.plan: 1. Schema: review in the status check, review_icon, review_svgs (jsonb), review_note. 2. WORKER_TOKEN check, GET/PATCH /api/worker/requests. 3. Status mapping (review shown as in-progress outside admin) and email rules. 4. /admin banner, review section, approve and request-changes actions. 5. scripts/request.mjs + root package script, .env.worker in .gitignore. 6. AGENTS.md section for Codex. 7. Owner: migration, WORKER_TOKEN on Vercel and in .env.worker. 8. Release minor.
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED v0.7.0, 2026-10-29] Migration and WORKER_TOKEN (Vercel + .env.worker) set by the owner. Checked on #22: start refused with 409 before Accept; after Accept, sync wrote icon-queue/22-email-test.md, start and review moved it to review and removed the file; Request changes put it back with the note, Approve made it ready and showed the release banner. [v0.7.1, 2026-10-29] The change note lost every letter s (regex typo) and duotone previews drew in one colour; both fixed.

entries.title: One daily email per developer instead of one email per request change
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: a developer who sends several requests gets an email for every request and every change, 'nije li to malo glupo?'. Chose one email a day.
entries.spec: No more received and in-progress emails (the page and API confirm a request at once; in-progress is an internal step). Accepted, declined (with reason), ready and shipped become rows in request_updates (request, kind, detail, created_at, sent_at) instead of emails. The daily cron (08:00 UTC) first records newly shipped requests, then sends one email per address with the latest change of each request since the last email, then marks the rows sent. Addresses that are unconfirmed or turned emails off get nothing (rows marked sent). The old admin button for shipped emails goes away. [2026-10-29, owner] /admin gets 'Send update emails now' (with how many changes for how many developers wait) for after a batch of work; an address mailed in the last 20 hours (email_settings.last_sent_at) is skipped by the morning cron, so nobody gets two in a day; its newer changes wait for the next email. Risk: news reaches a developer up to a day later. Out of scope: choosing the hour, a weekly option.
entries.plan: 1. request_updates table. 2. changeStatus and the shipped check record updates instead of mailing; drop the received and in-progress emails. 3. Digest sender and email text; cron runs shipped check + digest. 4. Remove the admin button. 5. Docs: page, icon-requests.md, README, settings label. 6. Release minor; check with a test request.

entries.title: Release to npm from /admin through GitHub Actions
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: can the npm release be started from the admin panel once everything is approved? Today it is a manual checklist with a passkey 2FA publish in the owner's terminal; release.json says 0.2.0 but npm still has 0.1.0, so 13 approved request icons (#4-#16) wait. 'ajmo složiti automatiku preko githuba'.
entries.spec: A GitHub Actions workflow npm-release.yml (workflow_dispatch, input bump: patch|minor) publishes @vectilume/icons and @vectilume/react with npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no npm token, no OTP, provenance). It reads the approved request ids from the site (worker token as a GitHub secret), sets the version from npm latest + bump, runs validate and tests, builds with build-release limited to approved request icons (an icon linked to a request that is not ready and not yet on npm stays out of the package), publishes both packages, commits release.json, tags npm-v<version> (web tags v* are taken) and tells the site to record the shipped requests for the update email. /admin gets 'Release to npm' (patch or minor) that dispatches the workflow through the GitHub API (GITHUB_TOKEN on Vercel: fine-grained, this repo, Actions read/write) and shows the last run with its result and link. Codex: pnpm request review also commits the icon (3 SVGs + collection file) and pushes to main, so CI sees it; one request at a time. Risks: npm staged publishing may still ask for approval on npmjs.com; drafts in review show in the web catalog before approval. Out of scope: visual diff in CI (the owner reviews the SVGs in /admin), changelog for npm.
entries.plan: 1. build-release: allowed request ids (env), keep published ones. 2. GET /api/worker/requests?status=ready and POST /api/worker/shipped (record only). 3. .github/workflows/npm-release.yml. 4. /admin button and last-run status. 5. request review commits and pushes; AGENTS.md. 6. Owner: trusted publisher on npmjs.com for both packages, GITHUB_TOKEN on Vercel, VECTILUME_WORKER_TOKEN as a GitHub secret. 7. Release web minor; first npm release from the button (0.2.0 with #4-#16).
entries.deploy_note: [DEPLOYED web v0.9.0 + v0.9.1, 2026-10-29] Owner set the npm trusted publisher (GitHub Actions, npm-release.yml, direct publish allowed) on both packages, VECTILUME_WORKER_TOKEN as a GitHub secret and GITHUB_RELEASE_TOKEN on Vercel. v0.9.0 shipped the workflow with a YAML error (an unquoted "authorization: " in a run line), so dispatch answered 422 and /admin showed an error page; v0.9.1 fixed both. [NPM 0.2.0, 2026-10-29] First release from the /admin button (minor): approved requests 4-16, validate and tests passed, both packages published with provenance and live on npm after ~5 min; 848 icons, 13 from requests. The commit step failed (release.json already said 0.2.0, nothing to commit), so the tag npm-v0.2.0 and the shipped record (13) were done by hand; the workflow now skips an empty commit.

entries.title: Admin: modern dark dashboard with charts and motion
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29, with a reference screenshot of a dark admin template: 'želim ovako moderan tamni admin dio uz animacije, grafove ako može i sve to'.
entries.spec: Only /admin changes; the public site stays light. Dark navy theme scoped to the admin page (own tokens in admin.module.css), a sidebar with section links (Overview, Review, Requests, Tokens) and sign out that becomes a top bar on phones. Overview: KPI cards with Vectilume icon chips and numbers that count up, each with what changed in the last 7 days; an area chart of requests and new tokens per day over the last 30 days (one axis, both are counts per day; hover crosshair with tooltip; table fallback for screen readers); a ring with the share of accepted requests that shipped and a bar per status. Cards, bars and lines animate in once on load; prefers-reduced-motion turns all motion off. Every existing action (accept, status, review, release, update emails, revoke) keeps its form and server action unchanged. Charts are hand-written SVG in small client components, no chart library. Out of scope: date range picker, light mode toggle for admin.
entries.plan: 1. Daily series query (Europe/Zagreb days) and 7-day deltas. 2. Dark admin tokens and layout with sidebar. 3. KPI cards with count-up. 4. Area chart and status ring/bars client components. 5. Restyle requests, review cards, tokens table, banners and login. 6. Typecheck, lint, look at it in the browser; release web minor.

entries.title: Designed HTML emails: confirmation link and the daily request update
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: 'složi vizualno privlačne email template ... da korisniku lijepo izgleda na mailu'.
entries.spec: Both emails get an HTML version next to the plain text (Resend sends both). Table layout with inline styles so Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail render it the same; light card on the site's grey, brand blue (#155bd0 / #2563eb, #93c5fd), system font stack, max 560 px, readable on phones. Confirmation: logo, short text, a 'Get my token' button and the link as text. Preheader text for inbox previews. entries.title: Sign in to /admin with a link mailed to the owner
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: 'nismo li rekli da prijava ide email pa magic link ili token? sad je samo token?' The email link existed only for developers on /request-icons; /admin took only ADMIN_TOKEN, which the owner had to dig out of Vercel and which leaked into a chat. 'da upiši i napravi'.
entries.spec: /admin sign-in asks for an email first. Only ADMIN_EMAIL (Vercel env) gets a one-time link (/admin?login=<code>, 15 minutes, used once, only the SHA-256 stored in admin_logins, at most 3 per hour per IP); every other address gets the same answer and nothing is sent. The token form stays as a fallback under 'Use the admin token instead' in case email fails. The link email uses the designed layout. Risk: without ADMIN_EMAIL set, only the token works (the form says so). Out of scope: several admins, sessions list.

Used for the /admin loading fallback and the requests list on /request-icons. Out of scope: button-sized inline spinners.

entries.title: Icon studio: a vector editor for Vectilume icons in the browser
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: 'stvarni svg ikona design studio za edit postojećih ikona i kreiranje novih u webu' (planned earlier in docs/web-features.md, points 1, 2 and recommendation 4). Owner's choices: developers use it from the start (phase 2 #icon-studio-proposals), a real vector editor (not code-first), the outline is drawn by hand and duotone/solid are helped (phase 3 #icon-studio-styles).
entries.spec: New page /studio (and /studio?icon=<icon> to open an existing icon; the catalog inspector links there with Edit in studio). 24x24 canvas with the 2-22 keyline, 1-unit grid, snapping to 0.25, zoom and pan. Tools: select/move, direct select (anchors and bezier handles), pen (click = corner, drag = smooth), line, rectangle with corner radius, circle, ellipse; delete, duplicate, nudge with arrows, undo/redo, layer list with order. Paths are parsed into absolute segments that keep their type (L, C, Q, A, Z), so shapes you do not touch keep their exact source; edited numbers round to 2 decimals. SVG code panel synced both ways (edit code -> canvas, draw -> code). Live checks while drawing: validateSvg from @vectilume/tooling (moved to a browser-safe entry) plus studio checks for the 2-22 keyline and anything closer than 0.5 to the gloss. Preview at 16/20/24/32/48 on light and dark, next to neighbouring icons of the same collection. Export: copy or download the SVG. Phase 1 has no saving to the library; that is phase 2. Risks: arcs are edited by end points and radius only; very complex paths may be slow to hit-test. Out of scope here: accounts, submitting, solid auto-derivation.
entries.plan: 1. Browser-safe validator entry in tooling. 2. Path model: parse/serialize SVG elements and path d (absolute, typed segments). 3. Editor state with undo/redo. 4. Canvas: grid, keyline, shapes, selection, anchors/handles, snapping, zoom. 5. Tools: select, direct select, pen, line, rect, circle, ellipse. 6. Code panel two-way sync, layers, inspector. 7. Live checks + previews. 8. Open existing icons (/studio/<icon>, all three styles as tabs). 9. Tests for the path model; release minor. [2026-10-29, done] Path model with typed absolute segments (round-trip test over every library path), shapes path/rect/circle/ellipse plus read-only transformed groups; one Select tool for moving shapes and dragging anchors/handles (anchor carries its handles), pen with corner/curve/close, line, rect (radius 3 by default), circle, ellipse; undo/redo (100 steps), duplicate, delete point/shape, curve/straight point, closed toggle, order; paint per style (outline stroke/filled detail, duotone primary stroke/secondary fill/primary fill, solid even-odd); Gloss is marked by hand per shape (the SVG has no place for it) and kept through code edits and the draft; checks = validateSvg + keyline + Gloss gap sampled every 0.1 by the browser; previews 16-48 light/dark and neighbours from the same group; draft of a new icon in localStorage; copy/download per style. Duotone/solid tabs offer Start from the outline (copy) until #icon-studio-styles.

entries.title: Icon studio: developers propose new icons and edits, the owner approves
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: developers use the studio from the start; proposals go through the owner's approval (docs/web-features.md points 1 and 2).
entries.spec: Signed-in developers (the same token/email as /request-icons) submit from the studio: a new icon (name, collection, group, keywords, three styles) or an edit of an existing one (one or all styles). Submitting requires accepting that the contribution is MIT. Stored in a new icon_proposals table with the SVGs; checks must pass before sending. /admin gets a Proposals section with old/new side by side (and overlaid) at several sizes; approve commits the SVGs and the collection entry to main through the GitHub Contents API (token with contents write), so it ships with the next npm release; ask for changes with a note; decline with a reason. Statuses and the daily update email reuse request_updates. Name is public API: the owner can rename before approving. Out of scope: author credits in the manifest (later), voting.
entries.plan: 1. Schema icon_proposals. 2. Submit API + studio submit dialog with MIT consent. 3. Admin proposals view with diff. 4. Approve -> GitHub commit; changes asked; declined. 5. Emails through the digest. 6. Release minor.

entries.title: Icon studio: duotone and solid helped from the outline
entries.summary: Owner, 2026-10-29: the outline is drawn by hand, duotone and solid are helped and then fixed by hand.
entries.spec: Duotone tab: mark closed shapes as 'body', the studio builds the duotone (secondary fill under, primary strokes on top, gloss stays a primary stroke). Solid tab: a suggested solid from the outline (strokes offset by 0.875 into filled silhouettes, gloss and inner details as cut-outs) using a geometry library (paper.js + offset or Clipper), opened in the editor for manual fixing. Each tab stays editable; regenerating asks before overwriting manual changes. Out of scope: perfect solids for every icon; the suggestion is a starting point.
entries.plan: 1. Body flag and duotone builder. 2. Pick and add the geometry library. 3. Solid suggestion. 4. Overwrite guard. 5. Release minor.
